episodes.212791: A stationary frontal boundary as well as both a Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic coast sea breeze combined with plentiful diurnal instability to produce robust thunderstorms across northeast FL during the afternoon and evening hours. Along with isolated severe thunderstorm activity, PWATs around 1.8 inches and slow moving/training convection resulted in very heavy rainfall and localized minor flooding.
episodes.213024: A broad surface low moved eastward across the northeast Gulf waters and across the Florida peninsula as a mid to upper level shortwave moved eastward across southern Georgia to the Georgia coast. Very high moisture levels for this time of the year were indicated by PWATs around 1.80 inches measured by the KJAX 05/13/2026 00Z Upper Air Sounding. Moist airmass and isentropic lift from the shortwave aloft developed heavy convergent rain showers with isolated thunderstorms along the coast just north of Jacksonville to Kingsland, St Marys, Cumberland Island, Jekyll Island to the Brunswick area beginning in the evening on May 12th into the morning of May 13th.
episodes.213582: A shortwave disturbance pushing across the eastern gulf interacting with a quasi-stationary surface frontal boundary extending across the peninsula generated a cluster of thunderstorms that produced a strong marine gust near Hudson Beach Park.
episodes.213583: A quasi-stationary surface boundary draped west to east across the northern peninsula and an approaching upper-level disturbance created an environment of favorable shear and instability that produced 2 EF-0 tornadoes near Hudson and Shady Hills in Pasco County.
episodes.213824: A moist and moderately unstable airmass along a cold front moving through the region  supported development of thunderstorms across southeast Louisiana late afternoon and evening of May 11th. Although weak low-level flow limited the overall severe-weather organization, locally heavy rainfall occurred in Baton Rouge metro as well as a brief tornado and associated wind damage in St. James Parish near Grand Point and Paulina.
episodes.213959: A dry microburst formed over the Tucson metro the afternoon of May 12th. This dry microburst caused roof damage to a large steel warehouse building. With this microburst, there was a recorded wind gust of 56 mph.

episodes.214424: On May 12th, the San Juan streamer persisted over the same areas across the San Juan metro area and nearby counties, leaving between 1 and 2 inches of rain during the mid-afternoon hours.

A brief, weak EF-0 tornado touched down in the community of Paulina, LA causing minor uplift of shingles on two homes. The tornado tracked north-northeast from Lena Street to Angelle Street at around 8 miles per hour before it was estimated to have lifted. This damage was collocated with a tight tornado vortex signature visible on TMSY doppler radar. No additional damage was identified via reports or aerial imagery. Time estimated by radar.

A storm exhibiting supercell characteristics for multiple hours while offshore moved ashore with a tornado estimated to have touched down around 1814 UTC (2:14 PM EDT) near Hudson in Pasco County, while continuing to exhibit a rotational signature via |KTBW WSR-88D and TTPA TDWR. Damage was initially observed along Saltwater Blvd, where a tree branch was snapped and fell onto a power line. Additional damage points were noted further east along Saltwater Blvd, with two homes suffering partial roof damage or loss. Additional homes suffered various degrees of roof, lanai or carport damage at points northward across Puffin, Heron and Curlew Lanes, while tree damage was noted across nearby Osprey and Gull Lanes. The tornado then crossed U.S. Hwy 19 before the radar signature became increasingly disorganized shortly thereafter, and it is likely that the tornado dissipated sometime around 1819 UTC (2:19 PM EDT) between Whitby Road and Lakeshore Blvd after traveling for just over one mile. Maximum peak wind of 85 mph.

The development of a second circulation became apparent west of Shady Hills around 20 minutes after the circulation associated with the Hudson tornado weakened, and it is estimated that a tornado touched down near Gladwin Avenue to the west of East Road |at approximately 1843 UTC (2:43 PM EDT). Damage from this tornado consisted largely of snapped tree limbs and branches, although a large tree was uprooted and downed onto a mobile home along Eden Avenue near the intersection of East Road. The tornado moved very slowly east and east-southeast while appearing to exhibit a bit of a binary interaction with the remnant circulation that produced the Hudson tornado that was located to its east, before radar indicated it likely dissipated around 1848 UTC (2:48 PM EDT), less than one mile from where it is estimated to have touched down. Maximum peak wind of 85 mph.
